one_liner: Slack has a broad, well-documented Web API with OAuth 2.0 and free developer sandboxes, plus an official hosted MCP server at mcp.slack.com.
auth_notes: Users go through the OAuth 2.0 flow to obtain user/bot tokens. Tokens are bearer tokens sent in the Authorization header. Bot and user tokens are also issued at app creation for your own workspace, which fits the API_KEY category.
access_notes: Anyone can create an app and get tokens. The free Developer Program provides a sandbox with Slack features, so no paid plan is needed. Workflow apps built with the Deno SDK and Workflow Builder need a paid plan, but the Web API does not. Distributing an app to other workspaces involves Slack's distribution and directory process.
blocker_notes: No major blocker. Slack's MCP server is limited to internal or directory-published apps.

evidence.quote: In order to obtain other users' tokens, you'll need to send users through the OAuth 2.0 authentication flow
When creating an app for the first time, you'll be given your own user and bot token while going through the app creation process.
All developers can provision a basic sandbox.
Join the Developer Program and provision a sandbox with access to all Slack features for free.
Slack API methods are accessible over HTTP, so the world is your oyster.
Since Slack hosts and manages the MCP Server, handling the tool logic on your behalf, implementing the connection is simple.
Slack only permits MCP on internal apps and directory-published apps, so an app built in your own workspace qualifies.
